facts: For a velocity–time graph in m/s against seconds, the area under the curve is a **distance** in metres.
Write the model as a definite integral before calculating: total change $=\int_{a}^{b}R(t)\,dt$.
A region bounded by a curve and an axis, both measured in metres, has an area in $\text{m}^{2}$.
Multiply a cross-sectional area in $\text{m}^{2}$ by a length in metres to get a volume in $\text{m}^{3}$.
Where the rate is negative the quantity is falling, so that part of the integral is subtracted.
Distance travelled adds the areas above and below the axis, while displacement subtracts them.
An area lying below the $x$-axis gives a negative integral, so take its absolute value for a physical size.
To find an unknown limit, set the definite integral equal to the given total and solve for it.
steps: Write the quantity as a definite integral
Interpret the answer with its practical unit

foundation.solution_text:
The distance travelled is the area under the velocity–time graph.
$\int_{0}^{4}3t^{2}\,dt$
$=\left[t^{3}\right]_{0}^{4}$
$=64-0$
$=64\text{ m}$

The distance travelled is the area under the velocity–time graph.
$\int_{0}^{6}\left(8t-t^{2}\right)dt$
$=\left[4t^{2}-\frac{t^{3}}{3}\right]_{0}^{6}$
$=144-72$
$=72\text{ m}$

The volume added is the area under the rate–time graph.
$\int_{0}^{5}(20+6t)\,dt$
$=\left[20t+3t^{2}\right]_{0}^{5}$
$=100+75$
$=175\text{ L}$

The fuel used is the area under the rate–time graph.
$\int_{0}^{3}\left(3t^{2}+4\right)dt$
$=\left[t^{3}+4t\right]_{0}^{3}$
$=27+12$
$=39\text{ L}$

The channel floor lies below ground level, so the integral is negative and the area is its absolute value.
$\int_{-4}^{4}\left(\frac{x^{2}}{4}-4\right)dx$
$=\left[\frac{x^{3}}{12}-4x\right]_{-4}^{4}$
$=\left(\frac{16}{3}-16\right)-\left(-\frac{16}{3}+16\right)$
$=-\frac{32}{3}-\frac{32}{3}$
$=-\frac{64}{3}$
The cross-sectional area is $\frac{64}{3}\text{ m}^{2}$.

development.solution_text:
The rate is negative for $t>3$, so water leaves the tank after $3$ seconds and that area is subtracted.
$\int_{0}^{5}(6-2t)\,dt$
$=\left[6t-t^{2}\right]_{0}^{5}$
$=30-25$
$=5\text{ L}$
The tank finishes with $5$ litres more water than it started with.

$\int_{-4}^{4}\left(\frac{x^{2}}{2}-8\right)dx$
$=\left[\frac{x^{3}}{6}-8x\right]_{-4}^{4}$
$=\left(\frac{32}{3}-32\right)-\left(-\frac{32}{3}+32\right)$
$=-\frac{64}{3}-\frac{64}{3}$
$=-\frac{128}{3}$
The cross-sectional area is $\frac{128}{3}\text{ m}^{2}$.
$V=\frac{128}{3}\times 6$
$=256\text{ m}^{3}$

mastery.solution_text:
The volume stops rising when the rate reaches zero.
$12-3t=0$
$t=4$
$\int_{0}^{4}(12-3t)\,dt$
$=\left[12t-1.5t^{2}\right]_{0}^{4}$
$=48-24$
$=24\text{ ML}$
The reservoir is back to its starting volume when the net change is zero.
$12T-1.5T^{2}=0$
$1.5T(8-T)=0$
$T=8\text{ days}$

The sled stops when its velocity is zero.
$24-6t^{2}=0$
$t^{2}=4$
$t=2$
$\int_{0}^{2}\left(24-6t^{2}\right)dt$
$=\left[24t-2t^{3}\right]_{0}^{2}$
$=48-16$
$=32\text{ m}$
